A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same CPDstergm study. The main text, five figures, eleven tables, and three appendix topics support reliable comparison despite revised pagination and appendix headings.

before.justification: v2 reports original Monte Carlo simulations and analyses of MIT cellphone and stock-market data in Section 5, Tables 1–8, and Figures 2–5.

after.justification: v3 retains the original simulation results and real-data analyses in Section 5, including numerical comparisons and detected change points.

M1.justification: The STERGM pseudo-likelihood, weighted group-fused penalty, ADMM updates, thresholding, and BIC selection remain unchanged. Calling the transformed beta subproblem Group Lasso does not change its update equations.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same SBM and STERGM simulation scenarios, MIT cellphone interactions, and DJIA stock-return networks. Temporal-dependence conditions and nodal-attribute scenarios are retained.

E2.justification: The evaluated comparators remain gSeg and kerSeg. Their network-input and network-statistics-input variants remain in Tables 1–6, with the same comparator participation in both real-data analyses.

E3.justification: Simulation parameters, sample sizes, true change points, metrics, comparator settings, and real-data preprocessing match. The lambda grid, 200/20/20 optimization budgets, 90% threshold quantile, and spacing and endpoint rules are retained.

E4.justification: The temporal-dependence sweep, network-statistic complexity comparisons, alternative comparator inputs, and real-data studies remain. No ablation, robustness test, or additional analytical investigation is introduced or removed.

E5.justification: Both versions report means from ten Monte Carlo trials per simulation setting. Neither adds seed information, variability estimates, confidence intervals, or statistical tests comparing method performance.

E6.justification: All 90 numerical result rows in Tables 1–6 match. The real-data dates, traces, and detection markers also remain unchanged, including the five CPDstergm markers in Figure 5 and the three stock events emphasized in Table 8.

T1.justification: v3 adds a terminal-segment equality to the change-point definition. Section 3.3 revises the stated Newton-Raphson complexity from O(tau^3 p^3) to O(tau^2 p^2), and block-coordinate complexity from O((tau−1)^2 tau p) to O(tau(tau−1)p). The appendix update derivations remain equivalent.

C1.justification: The central contributions remain simultaneous change-point detection using STERGM and Group Fused Lasso, ADMM estimation, BIC selection, an R package, and successful simulated and real-data applications. Condensed summaries do not redefine these claims.

C2.justification: v3 adds an explanation contrasting the group penalty with elementwise L1 penalization. It removes qualifications concerning parameter-effect interpretation, the ad hoc localization guidelines, and potentially unfair comparisons with gSeg and kerSeg under temporal dependence. The future-extension limitations remain.

D1.justification: v3 removes the explicit E = n × n definition from Section 3.2 and the ordered network-vector formula from v2 Appendix A. These are documentation losses, not demonstrated implementation changes. Hyperparameters, preprocessing information, and the CPDstergm repository pointer remain.

R1.justification: v3 adds Alaiz et al. (2013), Blackburn and Handcock (2022), Matias and Miele (2017), and Snijders et al. (2010). These modestly expand the context for group fused lasso, ERGM specification, and dynamic-network models without changing the overall positioning.

P1.justification: v3 copyedits and condenses the abstract and numerous paragraphs, folds Section 2.4 into Section 2.3, and replaces lettered appendix references with Supplemental Materials. The six-section narrative and overall argument remain intact.

P2.justification: Figures and tables are resized or repositioned, captions are shortened, repeated nets./stats. table footnotes are removed, and event tables use shorter labels and acronyms. All five figures and eleven tables are retained.

improvement.justification: Tighter prose, added citations, the group-penalty explanation, and the terminal-segment clarification offer modest benefits. However, v3 removes the explicit fairness warning for the unchanged temporal-dependence comparisons and the ad hoc-guideline qualification, while omitting the dyad-count definition and explicit network-vector ordering. These losses modestly weaken interpretive caution and reproducibility, outweighing the editorial gains.
